issues.description: The problem text explicitly instructs students to use StringBuilder for the Animal.name attribute for performance (text says use StringBuilder), but the provided solution defines the name attribute as a String (private String name) and its getter/setter use String. This is an attribute type mismatch between the problem specification and the solution reference which could confuse students about the expected type and the signatures of the getter/setter they must implement.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the artifacts: either update the problem statement to require a String (and remove the StringBuilder instruction) or update the solution/template to declare the name field as a StringBuilder and adjust the constructor, getter, and setter to accept/return/modify a StringBuilder accordingly. Ensure tests and examples reflect the chosen type.

issues.description: There is an internal contradiction within the problem statement: the UML shows the Animal.name attribute as type String, while the textual instructions ask students to use StringBuilder for the name attribute. This inconsistency in the specification will confuse students about the correct attribute type to implement.
issues.suggestedFix: Resolve the contradiction in the problem statement: make the UML and the textual instruction consistent. Preferably state explicitly which type is required (String or StringBuilder) in both the UML and the text. If StringBuilder is required, update the UML to show name: StringBuilder; if not, remove the StringBuilder guidance from the text.
